items.q: What is the most common (m/c) cause of primary hypothyroidism on page 905?
items.exp: Under Primary Hypothyroidism: '1. Autoimmune hypothyroidism (m/c) AKA Hashimoto thyroiditis'. (Book p905)

items.q: Autoimmune hypothyroidism is associated with Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndromes (APS); clinicians should specifically check for ___ before initiating treatment.
items.exp: Autoimmune hypothyroidism is associated with APS-1/2; clinicians 'Should check for APS2 before treatment'. (Book p905)

items.q: A patient with undetected coexisting adrenal insufficiency (APS-2) is prescribed L-thyroxine without prior cortisol supplementation. What acute consequence is cautioned on page 905?
opts: Adrenal insufficiency: shock in children, profound adrenal insufficiency in adults
Sudden thyrotoxic crisis with hyperpyrexia and delirium
Acute hypocalcemic tetany from suppressed parathyroid reserve
items.exp: If L-thyroxine is given without cortisol supplementation in APS-2, it precipitates adrenal insufficiency: shock in children, and profound adrenal insufficiency in adults. (Book p905)

items.q: Match the pharmacologic agent causing hypothyroidism to its specific clinical characteristic — 1) Lithium 2) Interferon-alpha (IFN-α) 3) Amiodarone … A) Associated with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (DI) B) Drug-associated thyroid destruction (irreversible side effect) C) Can produce both hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism
items.exp: Lithium causes hypothyroidism and nephrogenic DI; IFN-α causes irreversible thyroid destruction; amiodarone can produce both hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism. (Book p905)

items.q: Regarding side effects of interferon-alpha (IFN-α): I Thyroid destruction is an irreversible side effect. II Flu-like syndrome is a reversible side effect.
opts: Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
I is false; II is true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Page 905 notes for IFN-α: 'Irreversible S/E: thyroid destruction' and 'Reversible S/E : Flu like syndrome'. (Book p905)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT listed under causes of primary hypothyroidism on page 905?
opts: Pituitary mass effect from lymphocytic hypophysitis
items.exp: Pituitary mass effect is a cause of secondary hypothyroidism, not primary hypothyroidism. (Book p905)

items.q: In secondary hypothyroidism due to a pituitary mass effect, what is the most common (m/c) underlying etiology listed?
items.exp: Under Secondary Hypothyroidism: 'Pituitary cause : No significant hypothyroidism; Primary Cause - MASS effect - (m/c) Lymphocytic hypophysitis'. (Book p905)

items.q: Assess secondary hypothyroidism from pituitary disease: I It characteristically causes severe, profound isolated hypothyroidism. II Its primary mechanism is mass effect, most commonly from lymphocytic hypophysitis.
opts: I is false; II is true
Both I and II are true
I is true; II is false
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Page 905 states: 'No significant hypothyroidism' for pituitary cause, and its primary cause is mass effect, most commonly lymphocytic hypophysitis. (Book p905)

items.q: A 2-month-old infant with a large hepatic hemangioma develops profound hypothyroidism requiring massive doses of levothyroxine. What is the mechanism of this consumptive hypothyroidism?
opts: Increased deiodinase-III expression in the hemangioma converting active hormone to reverse T3
Direct destruction of the infant thyroid follicles by hemangioma-derived antibodies
Failure of intestinal absorption of thyroid hormone due to splanchnic steal
Suppression of hypothalamic TRH secretion by circulating angiogenin
items.exp: Consumptive hypothyroidism in hemangioma is driven by increased deiodinase-III expression leading to decreased active hormones and increased reverse T3. (Book p905)

items.q: Consumptive hypothyroidism associated with hemangioma is mediated by increased expression of ___, which accelerates the formation of ___.
items.exp: Hemangioma -> ↑ Deiodinase-III expression -> ↓ Hormones (↑ formation of Reverse T3). (Book p905)

items.q: What is the primary underlying cause of congenital hypothyroidism on page 905?
items.exp: Under Congenital Hypothyroidism: 'mostly due to thyroid dysgenesis'. (Book p905)

items.q: Match the newborn physical sign of congenital hypothyroidism to its system — 1) Cranial sign 2) Gastrointestinal sign 3) Hepatic sign … A) Open posterior fontanelle B) Delay in passing meconium C) Prolonged physiological jaundice
items.exp: Features of congenital hypothyroidism listed on page 905 are: open posterior fontanelle, delay in passing meconium, and prolonged physiological jaundice. (Book p905)

items.q: Which of the following is NOT listed on page 905 as a feature of congenital hypothyroidism?
opts: Delay in passing meconium and prolonged physiological jaundice
Very little crying and excessive sleep
items.exp: Features of congenital hypothyroidism are open posterior fontanelle, delay in passing meconium, prolonged physiological jaundice, very little crying, and excessive sleep. (Book p905)
